Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Acute severe headache on the left side with associated nausea/vomiting and photophobia.
- Onset, duration, progression: Began midday today; symptoms developed over a few hours; duration currently several hours. Headache described as intense and worsened by movement.
- Associated symptoms: Visual aura (zig-zag lines) preceding headache; blurred vision; photophobia; nausea and two episodes of vomiting.
- History of present illness details: Headache is unilateral, throbbing, worsened by neck/head movement. No reported weakness, speech difficulties, numbness, balance problems, fever, or rashes.
- Prior similar episodes: Had a similar headache a few weeks ago lasting a couple of days; not previously diagnosed as migraine. Family history of migraines (mother). Mother also has underactive thyroid.
- Past medical history: No other medical history documented by patient.
- Medications: Microgynon (oral contraceptive) for contraception, duration 3 months.
- Social history: Works in fashion; high job stress; lives alone; currently not exercising; non-smoker; does not regularly drink alcohol.
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Relevant concerns: Worries about brain tumor; recent exposure to a friend’s mother who died of a brain tumor; concerned about serious pathology.

Objective:
- Vitals: Not documented in transcript.
- Physical examination findings: Not documented in transcript.
- Other: No objective exam results provided.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Migraine headache (likely migraine with aura)
   - Assessment (condition name): Migraine, likely with aura.
   - Differential diagnoses: Meningitis; Brain tumor (intracranial pathology). Note: Patient expressed concern about brain tumor; clinician noted these as considerations to rule out.
   - Investigations planned: Headache diary to identify triggers and patterns.
   - Treatment planned: 
     - Analgesics: Paracetamol; Co-codamol (dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Anti-inflammatories: Ibuprofen; Naproxen (dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Prophylaxis consideration: If headaches become more persistent, discussion about preventive (prophylactic) medications at follow-up.
   - Referrals: None at this time.
Follow-up:
- Return or contact urgently if symptoms worsen or do not improve within 2–3 days, if neck pain worsens, if new weakness or visual changes occur.
- Plan to discuss further management at next visit (approximately one week).
